title: $4,120 recoverable — $890 expires in 21 days
narrative: Approval files cases and nothing else. No price changes, no inventory moves, no customer contact — the whole downside of this decision is a marketplace saying no.
status_note: Decide · 9 in batch · $3,480 face value · $84 written off and logged · floor $25

proposal.recommendation: Filing 9 claims worth $3,480 returns $3,080 at our own historic win rates. 2 more sit staged on missing documents and file themselves when the evidence lands. $84 is written off — recorded as leakage, which is the number that argues for fixing the cause.

item_groups.label: Auto-claimable
item_groups.blurb: Deterministic test, evidence complete, and the downside of being wrong is a polite denial. This is the batch path.

item_groups.foot: Every row here files against a published window with the documents policy names. Nothing in this group requires a human to form an opinion — which is precisely why it is the first flow that could run itself.

item_groups.label: Evidence needed
item_groups.blurb: Sound claims with a document gap. Each files itself the moment the last item lands — never partially, never late.

rows.name: Damaged in warehouse · 4 units
rows.detail: Attribution is in their record; condition photographs sit in the 3PL portal. Needs condition photographs · 4 units.

rows.name: Inbound shortage · Walmart WFS
rows.detail: 6 units short on PO-4488; needs carrier proof of delivery and the bill of lading. Needs carrier POD + bill of lading.

item_groups.foot: A claim filed without its named evidence spends the window and returns a denial, which then costs an appeal. Staging is not delay; it is the only path that pays.
